F1.hypothesis: Valid multi-file changes commit cleanly with WAL journal records and expected hashes.

F2.hypothesis: Interruption before any file replacement leaves disk intact and transitions journal safely.

F3.hypothesis: Crash after partial file application is detected; journal correctly records PARTIALLY_APPLIED and recovers.

F4.hypothesis: TOCTOU check detects external edit before application and prevents silent overwrite (Invariant A).
F4.errorMessage: TOCTOU_DISK_MODIFICATION_DETECTED: Target src/App.tsx was modified externally between snapshot and application. Aborting transaction without overwriting.

F5.hypothesis: Concurrent edit during multi-file loop triggers TOCTOU abort without overwriting the conflicting file.

F6.hypothesis: Rollback refrains from overwriting external modification in crash window; marks CONFLICTED and backs up user file (Invariant B).

F7.hypothesis: Fresh process instance reads SQLite WAL journal and re-synchronizes state after abrupt process termination.

F8.hypothesis: Exclusive file lock blocks concurrent transaction; releases cleanly upon completion.

F9.hypothesis: Path sanitizer rejects traversal (..), absolute paths, UNC paths, and Windows drive letters (Invariant D).

F10.hypothesis: Missing paths or invalid inputs fail closed before touching disk.

F11.hypothesis: Running recovery repeatedly is idempotent and creates zero duplicate mutations (Invariant F).

F12.hypothesis: System detects user additions after partial crash, halts rollback, creates backup, and prevents data loss (Invariants A, B, G).

acceptanceScorecard.verdict: PASS — RECOVERABLE MULTI-FILE PROTOCOL VALIDATED (NOT A FULL ATOMIC FILESYSTEM TRANSACTION)
acceptanceScorecard.summary: Gate 2 Validated: All 12 scenarios passed with zero silent overwrites, zero silent data loss, and 100% preservation of external user edits during crash intervals. Crucial architectural realism: SQLite WAL provides ACID durability for metadata, but filesystem multi-file modifications remain a recoverable protocol rather than native transactional atomicity.
